purpose: This shows why a^2 + b^2 = c^2 using area. You cut and slide pieces of one square and see that nothing is lost, so the tilted square must equal the two small squares together.

stops.title: The big square
stops.text: A big square holds four blue copies of your right triangle and a tilted yellow square labelled c squared. There is nothing to drag on the figure. The sliders and the button on the right move everything.
stops.try: Look for the four blue triangles and the tilted yellow outline in the middle.

stops.title: Leg a
stops.text: Sets the length of the short side along the bottom. The big square, the triangles and the tilted square all resize to match.
stops.try: Slide it to 6 and see how thin the other triangle side looks.

stops.title: Leg b
stops.text: Sets the other leg. Together with Leg a it decides the long side c. Try different pairs and watch the readout at the bottom.
stops.try: Find legs where c comes out as a whole number, like 3 and 4.

stops.title: Slide the pieces
stops.text: Progress runs from 0 to 100 percent. At 0 the yellow shape is one tilted square c squared. At 100 three triangles have slid over and it is two squares, a squared and b squared. Same area, same pieces.
stops.try: Drag Progress slowly back and forth and watch the labels swap.

stops.title: Play the slide
stops.text: This button plays the slide for you. After it runs, the button turns into Put them back. The triangles only move. They never turn or stretch.
stops.try: Press it, then press it again to undo.

stops.title: What Next does
stops.text: Step 1 shows the 3, 4, 5 triangle. Step 2 slides the triangles. Step 3 gives a lopsided triangle (a = 5, b = 2). Step 4 makes both legs equal, which gives the diagonal of a square.

stops.title: Quick check
stops.text: Two questions: one finds a hypotenuse, one asks why the areas match. A wrong answer explains why.

teacher: Project step 2 and ask: the pieces only moved, so what must be true about the two yellow shapes? Students often think the theorem is only a formula for 3, 4, 5. Use step 3 with odd legs to show it works for any right triangle.
